channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Oil Set for Weekly Gain as Supply Risks Grow
item.description: Brent oil headed for a third weekly gain as attacks on Saudi Arabia raised the risk of wider Middle East supply disruptions. The flareup threatens to widen hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz, where crude exports have recovered to near prewar levels. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Modi Attacks Rahul Gandhi Over ‘Disorder’ Risk to India’s Image
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, saying attempts to create “disorder” at home risk damaging the country’s standing at a time of growing global economic and geopolitical tensions.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia

item.title: Suhasini Haidar on India’s Challenges
item.description: Suhasini Haidar, diplomatic editor for The Hindu, describes the police response to the “Cockroach” protests in Delhi and how assumptions are being challenged about India’s place in the world. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Plans Military Presence to Contain Next Round of Protests
item.description: French authorities are bracing for a new round of protests Saturday, rolling out the military to back up police in a bid to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s riots and reassure markets unnerved by the violence.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot

item.title: India Voter-Roll Protests Widen as Farmers Set to Join In
item.description: Indian farmers who helped force Prime Minister Narendra Modi into a rare policy retreat four years ago are set to join nationwide protests against a contentious overhaul of voter rolls on Friday, widening a movement challenging the country’s Election Commission.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia

item.title: Trump Seeks to Boost Republicans in Razor-Thin Iowa Senate Race
item.description: President Donald Trump traveled to Iowa on Thursday to boost Ashley Hinson, the Republican Senate candidate locked in a tight race with Democrat Josh Turek.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Aidan Williams

item.title: Musk Giving Tops $445 Million in Midterm Election Push for GOP
item.description: With a fresh infusion of cash to his super political action committee in the first two weeks of October, Elon Musk has now given more than $445 million in the current election cycle and become one of the biggest-ever contributors to such groups.
item.dc:creator: Bill Allison and Dana Hull

item.title: China Tech Repricing Deepens as Geopolitical Risks Mount
item.description: Bloomberg’s Anthony Stephens discusses how doubts over AI returns and mounting geopolitical friction are deepening the repricing across Chinese tech stocks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Election: Lula’s New Cell Phone Gives Him a Shot at Reelection
item.description: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stubbornly made a point of never wanting, or needing, a cell phone. A jaw-dropping election setback made him reconsider. The question now is whether it’s too late.
item.dc:creator: Beatriz Reis

item.title: Trump: Musk ‘Put Back’ Ukraine Starlink Access
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Celinda Lake, founder of Lake Research and a Democratic pollster whose firm has done polling for Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign, says Republicans are in deep trouble, but Democrats have a lot to prove. Evelyn Farkas, McCain Institute executive director and former deputy assistant secretary of defense for Russia, Ukraine and Eurasia, says it's a moral problem for the US that Starlink speeds were slowed while Ukrainians were trying to intercept missiles and drones targeting civilians. Aaron Lehman, president of the Iowa Farmers Union and fifth-generation farmer in Polk County, Iowa, says both diesel prices and tariffs have been devastating for farmers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Haiti Hostage Crisis Drags in El Salvador Elite Forces, Reports Say
item.description: El Salvador has sent 100 members of its special forces to Haiti in a bid to rescue four of its military personnel who were kidnapped by gangs in the troubled Caribbean nation, the Miami Herald and the Associated Press reported.
item.dc:creator: Jim Wyss

item.title: Lehman Says Diesel, Tariffs Have Been Devastating for Farmers
item.description: Aaron Lehman, president of the Iowa Farmers Union and fifth-generation farmer in Polk County, Iowa, says both diesel prices and tariffs have been devastating for farmers. Lehman says farmers have not felt that an Iowa voice has been standing up for them in Washington and says that while farmers need relief, temporary measures do not address the underlying causes of their financial strain. Lehman says agriculture has a monopoly problem that leaves farmers especially vulnerable when fertilizer supplies are disrupted. Lehman says he finds President Donald Trump's deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to try to lower diesel costs disturbing. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Farkas Says Starlink Slowdown Helped the Russians
item.description: Evelyn Farkas, McCain Institute executive director and former deputy assistant secretary of defense for Russia, Ukraine and Eurasia, says it's a moral problem for the US that Starlink speeds were slowed while Ukrainians were trying to intercept missiles and drones targeting civilians. Farkas says Russian President Vladimir Putin continues to signal openness to negotiations while maintaining his maximalist claims and continuing attacks on Ukrainians. Farkas says Putin is trying to get European countries to stop supporting Ukraine and says a diesel deal with President Donald Trump came out of a call between the two leaders. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lake Says Republicans in Trouble, Democrats Have a Lot to Prove
item.description: Celinda Lake, founder of Lake Research and a Democratic pollster whose firm has done polling for Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign, says Republicans are in deep trouble, but Democrats have a lot to prove. Lake says Republicans are in trouble with farmers as diesel prices remain elevated and trade policy is hurting farmers. Lake says Democrats are short of money, but sees potential for surprises in races around the country. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bolsonaro and Lula Tied Ahead of Brazil Runoff, Poll Shows
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva are tied just days before Brazil’s Sunday runoff election, a new poll showed.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati

item.title: Supreme Court Backs Republicans on New Hampshire Voter IDs
item.description: The US Supreme Court lifted a ruling that would have allowed use of student-ID cards to help show eligibility to vote in New Hampshire, siding with Republicans in a state where Democrats are defending a Senate seat next month.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: SpaceX-Tesla Merger (Podcast)
item.description:
Elon Musk has publicly endorsed a combination of SpaceX and Tesla, his two most valuable companies, in what would be the biggest corporate transaction ever attempted. There's a push to announce a deal by the first half of 2027, so that it closes during the current administration, according to people familiar with the matter, with the combined market value of the companies being around $3.7 trillion. Musk's endorsement comes at a moment of extraordinary influence for him, having repaired his relationship with President Donald Trump and tapped into fervent investor enthusiasm, but this advantage is not guaranteed to last.
On today's episode:
Max Chafkin, Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Reporter Jackie Reses, co-founder and CEO of Lead Brett Winton, Chief Futurist, ARK Investment Management Andra Timu, Bloomberg Reporter covering Romania on Russian Drones Attacking EU (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Selloff Deepens as AI Spending Worries Investors
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner Gene Munster, Invesco CIO & Co-Head of Fixed Income Rob Waldner, TD Cowen Senior Research Analyst Andrew Charles, Huntington Bancshares CEO & Chairman Stephen Steinour, Pivotal Advisors CEO & CIO Tiffany McGhee, Susquehanna Senior Equity Research Analyst Mehdi Hosseini, JPMorgan Asset Management, Global Alternatives Strategist Aaron Mulvihill, Alex Mill Chairman Mickey Drexler, Kroger CFO Dav Kennerley, & H/L Ventures Co-Founder & Managing Partner Oliver Libby. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New York City Council Votes to Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages by 2028
item.description: New York’s City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending a Central Park tourist staple dating to the 19th century after years of debate over the horses’ place on city streets.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias and Cameron Fozi

item.title: Top RFK Jr. Adviser Calley Means Resigns in Blow to MAHA
item.description: Calley Means, a top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., resigned Thursday, dealing a setback to the administration’s efforts to overhaul the US food system.
item.dc:creator: Kristina Peterson and Rachel Cohrs Zhang
